candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: maintain invasive devices using aseptic technique and implement measures that reduce healthcare-associated infection risk.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — central-line dressing integrity
candidate.educational_objective: Maintain central-line site protection by promptly replacing any dressing that becomes loose, damp, or visibly soiled using appropriate aseptic site-care technique rather than waiting for the routine interval or removing an otherwise needed catheter solely for dressing failure.

options.A: Replace the compromised dressing promptly using appropriate aseptic catheter-site care according to facility policy.
options.B: Leave it in place until the routine scheduled dressing change because looseness alone is not an indication for replacement.
options.C: Tape over the loose edges without reassessing or replacing the dressing because preserving the old dressing is preferred.
options.D: Remove the central venous catheter solely because the dressing is loose, even if the catheter remains clinically indicated and the site has no other complication.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC recommends replacing a catheter-site dressing whenever it becomes damp, loosened, or visibly soiled and covering catheter sites with sterile gauze or a sterile transparent semipermeable dressing. A loose dressing compromises the protective barrier and should not be left until the next routine interval. B and C fail to restore an intact dressing. D overreacts: a loose dressing requires prompt dressing replacement, but catheter removal is based on catheter necessity and complications rather than looseness of the dressing alone.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A central-line dressing that becomes loose should be replaced promptly with an intact sterile dressing using appropriate catheter-site care; looseness alone does not automatically require removal of a clinically necessary catheter.
candidate.source_document_title: Guidelines for the Prevention of Intravascular Catheter-Related Infections — Summary of Recommendations; Prevention Strategies
candidate.source_locator: Catheter Site Dressing Regimens: use sterile gauze or sterile transparent semipermeable dressing to cover the site; replace catheter-site dressing if it becomes damp, loosened, or visibly soiled (Category IB). Central-line maintenance recommendations also emphasize continued assessment of catheter necessity and insertion-site condition.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: Current CDC infection-control web guidance accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A nurse notes that a central venous catheter dressing has become loose and no longer fully covers the insertion site. What should the nurse do?
